transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC, Duration ~59 minutes. Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Diego Chan (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Rachel Lin (OptiRetail CTO), Samir Patel (OptiRetail ML Eng), Jenna Morris (OptiRetail Infra), Leo Kim (Product).

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Ava, i'll run the agenda. Diego and Priya from our SE team are here to dig into the performance stuff. Rachel, do you want to kick off with your high-level goals?

[00:12] Rachel: Sure, thanks. we're looking to replace our in-house LLM serving for product tagging and search re-rank. Peak traffic around Black Friday is the big worry, and we need predictable latency under 120ms p50 for short completions and throughput for concurrent sessions. We also have strict data residency and want VPC or on-prem options.

[00:31] Samir: Also interested in KV cache behavior - we rely on persistent context and fast warm starts. Quantization is something we'd consider to reduce cost but worried about quality hit.

[00:45] Diego: Okay great. quick outline: we'll walk Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs for runtime, batching & KV cache, impact of quantization on throughput/latency and accuracy, and then constraints for VPC/on-prem and noisy neighbor isolation. We'll sprinkle in a couple of numbers from our benches.

[01:05] Priya: just to set expectations, some of the numbers are workload-dependent; we'll explain distributions and how to run the benchmarks.

[01:18] Rachel: perfect.

[01:25] Diego: Starting with the runtime: Redwood's serving runtime has continuous batching and KV cache. In Hosted mode we multi-tenant pools by default which gives elastic capacity but there can be noisy neighbor effects during sudden spikes; we mitigate with auto-scaling and priority routing but it is not the same as dedicated GPU isolation.

[01:45] Jenna: can you quantify noisy neighbor? like are there CPU/GPU preemption events or just queueing delays?

[01:51] Diego: mostly queueing + scheduling delays. on multi-tenant hosts we schedule many small requests into shared GPUs and if a tenant suddenly pushes large batches, it can increase tail latency. we limit per-tenant concurrency and apply fair-queueing, but the observed effect is usually higher p95/p99 latency during extreme spikes. Typical p50/p95 numbers for our hosted 8k-token workloads: p50 70ms, p95 270ms - but depends on model and sequence length.

[02:20] Samir: Those p95 numbers are pretty wide. For us p95 needs to be under 500ms for interactive usage, but for checkout-critical flows we'd like p99 under 1s.

[02:32] Priya: With Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools - that removes noisy neighbor from other customers. you still have intra-customer noisy neighbor from other services on the same pool if you colocate multiple model endpoints, but you can allocate pools per workload to avoid that. Dedicated also allows pinned kernel selection and tuning for a given model and sequence length distribution which reduces variance.

[02:58] Leo: what's the throughput guarantee on Dedicated? can we set SLOs?

[03:03] Diego: We offer capacity-reserved contracts - you pick a pool size (e.g., 8x A100 equivalent) and get predictable throughput estimates. We'll provide throughput curves (tokens/sec) per model variant under continuous batching assumptions. For hard SLOs we recommend a small buffer (burst capacity) or an autoscale headroom config in the Dedicated plan. We also support preemption-safe fallback: if Dedicated runs out of capacity we can route to a compatible Hosted tier with longer latency but still available.

[03:31] Jenna: about KV cache: does Dedicated keep cache warm across requests better than Hosted?

[03:36] Priya: Yes, because Dedicated pools maintain longer-lived worker processes and you control request routing to keep affinity. Hosted uses eviction policies based on overall memory pressure; that means cold-starts for large KV caches can happen more often in multi-tenant. For your product tagging we saw up to 4-5x slower first-token latencies when a cache is cold.

[03:58] Samir: do you support pinned KV cache per customer in Hosted?

[04:02] Diego: We have tenant-aware caching where hot prefixes are prioritized, but pinning is a Dedicated feature. There is also prefix caching API you can use to pre-warm before peak windows.

[04:15] Rachel: batching - our team worries that aggressive batching to improve throughput will blow past latency SLOs. how do you handle dynamic batching?

[04:23] Priya: Redwood uses adaptive batching where we set a max batch size and a short batching window (ms) that trades latency vs throughput. For short-latency needs we tune to lower window and smaller max batch sizes. In Dedicated you can safely increase max batch sizes because you control pool contention, yielding much better token/sec without increasing p50 significantly. Example numbers from an internal test for a 4k-param model: Hosted continuous batching token/sec ~120k with p50 80ms p95 320ms; Dedicated tuned batcher token/sec ~210k with p50 85ms p95 190ms. The tail improves because scheduling is deterministic.

[05:10] Leo: quantization - what do you recommend for preserving quality while reducing memory?

[05:14] Diego: Our recommended path is 4-bit quantization plus selective higher-precision layers for sensitive layers (activation-aware quant). For many retrieval-augmented tasks you see minimal quality loss on top-k outputs. We provide quantization profiles and can run regression evals on your prompt set. Note: quantization can reduce memory and increase throughput but sometimes increases per-token latency slightly due to dequant/decompress costs - depends on kernels. On Dedicated we can tune kernel selection to favor quantized fast paths.

[05:47] Samir: can we run mixed precision? some of our models need float16 for top-k ranking.

[05:53] Priya: yes, mixed precision is supported. we recommend a canary where you run a subset of requests on quantized model and monitor quality regressions. we have eval tooling integrated to compare metrics like hit-rate, rerank MRR.

[06:08] Jenna: VPC/on-prem - what are the constraints for low-latency connections? we are hosted across us-east and eu-west and would like a VPC-peered option to minimize egress.

[06:18] Diego: For VPC Private deployments we can provision a private control plane with customer-managed networking or an on-prem option. Latency will depend on network RTT: we suggest colocating Dedicated pools in the same region as your app or using our VPC peering to avoid internet hops. For on-prem we provide an appliance image and a private runtime; the biggest work is ensuring GPUs and drivers match our supported matrix. We'll need bandwidth/egress numbers to size the cluster and to advise on model shard placement.

[06:48] Rachel: Are there compliance or audit impacts to routing fallback from Dedicated to Hosted? we have SOC2 and sensitive PII concerns.

[06:55] Ava: Good question. fallback routing can be restricted per-tenant; if you require strict isolation we can disable fallback to Hosted entirely and fail-open to local queues or autoscale the Dedicated pool. We also support customer-managed KMS and audit logs - we'll send SOC2 & KMS docs.

[07:13] Jenna: network egress - does Redwood ever route traffic outside the region during heavy load?

[07:19] Diego: By policy we prefer region-local routing. Fallback to cross-region is opt-in and only used for resiliency when you enable multi-region fallback. For Dedicated single-region setups we keep traffic in-region unless you ask otherwise.

[07:33] Samir: performance tuning: how do we benchmark ourselves? what artifacts do you need?

[07:39] Priya: ideal deliverables: sample prompt set, per-request token distribution, concurrency patterns (RPS, percentiles), and acceptable quality thresholds. We'll run both a Hosted synthetic pass and a Dedicated reserved-pool sim. We'll produce token/sec, latency curves, and KV cold-warm delta.

[07:56] Leo: can you show an example of KV cold vs warm?

[08:00] Diego: quick example: warm requests where KV has the context hit p50 60ms p95 120ms; cold-first-token where cache miss requires recompute brings p50 up to ~320ms on Hosted multi-tenant at our typical config. Dedicated tuned workers reduce that cold penalty to ~150-180ms. These are illustrative and depend on model size and KV memory footprint.

[08:23] Rachel: any gotchas around autoscaling on Dedicated? we dont want to pay for peak all year.

[08:29] Ava: Dedicated supports burst pools and autoscaling policies. you can commit to a base capacity and enable burst capacity for short windows. pricing is a mix of reserved + burst usage. We can show cost projections given your peak fraction.

[08:40] Samir: curious about SDK-level controls - can we force no-batching for some endpoints?

[08:46] Priya: yes, per-route config you can set batching mode to none or strict, and also set cache affinity hints.

[08:54] Jenna: security: what about SSO and RBAC for infra teams to access logs and debugging tools?

[08:59] Diego: we support SAML/SSO + granular RBAC, plus audit logs for inference requests. logs can be exported to your SIEM. For on-prem we can integrate with your IdP.

[09:12] Rachel: Great. Any quick recommendations?

[09:15] Priya: For your Black Friday requirement, our recommendation is start with a small Dedicated pool sized to handle base traffic with autoscale headroom and burst enabled for the peak window, keep critical flows pinned to dedicated endpoints (no fallback to Hosted), and run a canary quantization + batching test on a subset of requests to measure quality impact. Also pre-warm KV caches before expected peaks.

[09:38] Leo: sounds good. what's the timeline to get the benchmark back?

[09:42] Diego: Once we get your prompt sets and request distribution Samir - we'll run a dedicated sim and return results in 3 business days.

[09:49] Ava: Recap of next steps: Diego will run the throughput sim; Samir to send prompts; Jenna to get network constraints; Ava to send pricing and security docs. We'll schedule an on-prem feasibility after the initial bench.

[09:59] Rachel: thanks everyone, that was helpful.

[10:02] [meeting ends]
